topIssues.title: tryStorageLayoutLookup in AccountAccessParser should be able to handled tightly packed variables
topIssues.author: blmalone
topIssues.body:
> We should make whatever decoding approach we come up with mirror what it looks like in tenderly.



Right now the `tryStorageLayoutLookup` function has the following function signature: 
```solidity
function tryStorageLayoutLookup(string memory _contractName, bytes32 _slot, bytes32 _oldValue, bytes32 _newValue)
        internal
        view
        returns (DecodedSlot memory decoded_)
```

In reality, many changes can occur in a single slot, so we could change this function to return an array: 
```solidity
function tryStorageLayoutLookup(string memory _contractName, bytes32 _slot, bytes32 _oldValue, bytes32 _newValue)
        internal
        view
        returns (DecodedSlot[] memory decoded_)
```

right now, if we detected a slot that is shared, we don't try to decode it. Completing this issue would require being able to decode these shared slots: 

```solidity
            if (isSlotShared(layout, _slot)) {
                return DecodedSlot({kind: "", oldValue: "", newValue: "", summary: "", detail: ""});
            }
```

topPRs.title: feat: Osaki Sepolia L1 + L2 ProxyAdmin owner transfers (097, 098)
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Two stacked tasks that move the **Osaki Sepolia** (chainId `9111973`) chain
ownership from the standard Sepolia L1PAO Safe to the new owner Safe
`0xFB0F8937A0d6999C67E8a01310eBf7fe1859205F` (and its L1-to-L2 alias on L2).

- **`097-osaki-l1-ownership-transfers`** — `TransferOwners` template
  - `ProxyAdmin.transferOwnership(0xFB0F...)`
  - `DisputeGameFactoryProxy.transferOwnership(0xFB0F...)`
  - `DelayedWETH` (v1.5.0) is post-U16 / not ownable → the template logs a
    "not ownable, not performing transfer" line and produces no state change.
- **`098-osaki-l2pao-transfer`** — `TransferL2PAOFromL1` template
  - `OptimismPortal.depositTransaction` targeting the L2 ProxyAdmin predeploy
    (`0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000018`) with
    `transferOwnership(alias(0xFB0F...))`.
  - Aliased L2 owner: `0x0C208937a0D6999c67E8A01310ebF7fE18593170`.
  - Stacked after `097`. A `stateOverride` pre-applies the L1 transfer so the
    template's `proxyAdmin.owner() == newOwnerToAlias` check passes when
    simulating in isolation.

Osaki is not in the public `superchain-registry`; both tasks use
`fallbackAddressesJsonPath` with chain addresses sourced from `op-deployer`
state. The chain reuses OP Sepolia's standard `SuperchainConfig`
(`0xC2Be75506d5724086DEB7245bd260Cc9753911Be`), so
`TransferOwners._validateSuperchainConfig` is satisfied.

The L1PAO is a 2-of-2 nested Safe (FoundationUpgradeSafe + SecurityCouncil).
All three Safe nonces are pinned via `stateOverrides` so the domain/message
hashes in each `VALIDATION.md` are reproducible — signers must re-verify the
live nonces with `cast call <safe> "nonce()"` before signing and bump the
overrides + re-simulate if anything has advanced.

## Test plan

Both tasks simulate cleanly on Sepolia:

- [x] `just simulate foundation` for 097 and 098 produces the hashes recorded
      in each `VALIDATION.md`.
- [x] `just simulate council` for 097 and 098 produces the hashes recorded in
      each `VALIDATION.md`.
- [x] `just simulate-stack sep 097-osaki-l1-ownership-transfers <foundation|council>`
      passes the TaskManager hash check.
- [x] `just simulate-stack sep 098-osaki-l2pao-transfer <foundation|council>`
      passes the TaskManager hash check (stack: 097 → 098).
- [x] Observed L1 state diff for 097: ProxyAdmin slot `0x00` and
      DisputeGameFactoryProxy slot `0x33` flip from the old to the new owner.
- [x] Observed L1 state diff for 098: OptimismPortalProxy params slot bump
      with `_gasLimit = 0x30d40 (200,000)`; L2 effect is verified post-
      execution per the manual steps in `098/VALIDATION.md`.

## Pre-signing checklist (for reviewers)

- [ ] Confirm `0xFB0F...205F` is the intended new owner (verified on-chain as
      a 1-of-12 Gnosis Safe v1.4.1).
- [ ] Confirm DGF + ProxyAdmin should be transferred together (DelayedWETH is
      non-ownable and skipped automatically).
- [ ] Re-verify the three live Safe nonces against `cast call <safe> "nonce()"`
      and update the `stateOverrides` + re-simulate if any have advanced
      since the values pinned in `config.toml`.

topPRs.title: feat: Ink SystemConfig owner transfers to FoundationOperationsSafe (eth/055, sep/101)
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
## Description

Transfers ownership of the Ink `SystemConfigProxy` on both networks from the current Ink-controlled owner Safe to the Optimism **FoundationOperationsSafe**, using the existing `TransferSystemConfigOwnership` template (one chain per task):

| Task | Chain | SystemConfigProxy | Current owner (signer) | New owner (FOS) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `eth/055-ink-transfer-system-config-owner` | Ink (57073) | [`0x62C0a111929fA32ceC2F76aDba54C16aFb6E8364`](https://etherscan.io/address/0x62C0a111929fA32ceC2F76aDba54C16aFb6E8364) | `0xBeA2Bc852a160B8547273660E22F4F08C2fa9Bbb` | [`0x9BA6e03D8B90dE867373Db8cF1A58d2F7F006b3A`](https://etherscan.io/address/0x9BA6e03D8B90dE867373Db8cF1A58d2F7F006b3A) |
| `sep/101-ink-transfer-system-config-owner` | Ink Sepolia (763373) | [`0x05C993e60179f28bF649a2Bb5b00b5F4283bD525`](https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x05C993e60179f28bF649a2Bb5b00b5F4283bD525) | `0xBeA2Bc852a160B8547273660E22F4F08C2fa9Bbb` | [`0x837DE453AD5F21E89771e3c06239d8236c0EFd5E`](https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x837DE453AD5F21E89771e3c06239d8236c0EFd5E) |

### Input verification

- Current owners verified on-chain: `cast call <SystemConfigProxy> "owner()(address)"` returns `0xBeA2Bc852a160B8547273660E22F4F08C2fa9Bbb` on both networks (the same 3-of-5 Safe, v1.3.0, identical owner set on both networks).
- `SystemConfigProxy` addresses verified against the superchain-registry ([mainnet/ink.toml](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/blob/main/superchain/configs/mainnet/ink.toml), [sepolia/ink.toml](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/blob/main/superchain/configs/sepolia/ink.toml)).
- New owners match `FoundationOperationsSafe` in `src/addresses.toml` (`[eth]` / `[sep]`).
- Signer Safe nonces pinned via `stateOverrides` (eth: 50, sep: 4 — on-chain values at task creation) so the VALIDATION.md hashes are reproducible.

### Simulation

Both tasks simulate successfully (`just simulate` and `just simulate-stack`): the only state changes are the `SystemConfig` owner slot (`0x33`) flipping to the FOS and the signer Safe nonce bump. Domain hashes were additionally reproduced independently with `cast keccak` (see each VALIDATION.md).

Note: `just simulate-stack sep 101-...` currently fails in unrelated task `097-osaki-l1-ownership-transfers` — its pinned FoundationUpgradeSafe nonce (70) has drifted behind the live value (72) on main. The sep/101 single-task simulation passes.

## Harness fix: EIP-7702 delegated EOA owners

On **mainnet**, one owner of the Ink Safe (`0x6a0A93Cd6d6FB7a36bF6234ef4650Bf9474e7682`) is an EIP-7702 delegated EOA: its code is the 23-byte delegation designator `0xef0100…`. `MultisigTask` classified any owner with code as a child Safe and called `nonce()` on it, which reverts (the delegation target exposes no Safe interface) — making every task signed by this Safe impossible to simulate.

This PR adds `Utils.isEip7702DelegatedEOA` (exact designator check: 23 bytes, `0xef0100` prefix) and excludes such owners from:
- the owner-Safe nonce safety checks in `_overrideState`, and
- the Safe branch of `_incrementOwnerNonce` (account nonce is used instead, as for any EOA).

Covered by a new unit test (`test_isEip7702DelegatedEOA`); `vm.etch` itself rejects malformed designators, so only valid designators can exist on-chain. The eth/055 simulation exercises this path end-to-end against live mainnet state. Other `code.length > 0` owner-classification sites (`isNestedSafe`, `_collectAllSiblingDataToSign`) are nested-task-only and not hit by these tasks; they can be hardened in a follow-up.

### Testing

- `test/libraries/Utils.t.sol`: 13/13 pass (includes new 7702 test)
- `test/tasks/MultisigTask.t.sol`: 21/21 pass
- Remaining fork suites fail locally only with `historical state is not available` from the public RPC — identical failures on unmodified `main` (verified via `git stash`); CI archive RPCs are authoritative.

## Checklist

- [x] Simulation completes successfully (no reverts) — single-task for both; stacked for eth
- [x] State changes reviewed and documented in each VALIDATION.md
- [x] README.md complete for both tasks
- [x] VALIDATION.md with domain/message/safe-tx hashes for both tasks
- [x] Task status set to DRAFT, NOT READY TO SIGN
- [x] No TODOs left in task files

topPRs.title: feat(eip712): enable eip712 typed data to be provided to eip712sign lib
topPRs.author: blmalone
topPRs.body:
### TL;DR

Add support for EIP-712 structured data signing for Safe transactions, allowing signers to use tools that support typed data signing.

### What changed?

- Added a new environment variable `EIP712_ENCODED_DATA_TO_SIGN` to control whether to use EIP-712 typed data JSON for signing or just the domain and message hashes (default)
- Implemented `encodeEIP712Json` to generate properly formatted EIP-712 JSON for Safe transactions
- Renamed and enhanced `getDomainAndMessageHashFromEncodedTransactionData` to `getDomainAndMessageHashFromDataToSign` to handle both formats
- Updated the MultisigTask to support both signing methods while ensuring they produce the same hashes
- Added comprehensive tests for the new EIP-712 JSON signing functionality
